lead: A neighbourhood in transformation, between warehouses turned into creative spaces and the works for the new station.
text: Its name comes from the sagreres: in the 11th century, Abbot Oliba agreed with the nobles to create a zone of thirty paces around the churches where peasants and their goods would be safe, and from this arose a protected area of the village of Sant Martí de Provençals. Although it now belongs to the Sant Andreu district, it never formed part of the old municipality of Sant Andreu de Palomar.

Today it lives alongside the works for the future Barcelona-La Sagrera station, under way since 2009, and cultural and creative spaces such as the Nau Ivanow and the Nau Bostik, the Parc de la Pegaso, the largest in the neighbourhood, and the Mercat de Felip II. With 31,247 inhabitants in 0.99 km², it is a neighbourhood in transition, where the surroundings change with each phase of the works.
housing: Blocks of flats from different periods, with former industrial warehouses converted to new uses.
